2015 Willmore Mountain Goat Surveys  
Background 
Mountain goats in Alberta live in small, isolated populations which are highly vulnerable to 
overharvest.  In the mountain complexes in and around the Willmore Wilderness Park, only 
three complexes have had a large enough herd of goats for a sustainable hunt in the past few 
years (i.e. more than 50 goats observed). 
Survey Method 
To achieve a minimum total count of mountain goats, alpine ridges and exposed cliff faces along 
river canyons were flown counter clockwise using a Bell 206B Jet Ranger helicopter.  Surveys 
were conducted in the early morning and in the evening when goats were most active and 
winds most favorable.  Where necessary, tall cliff faces were flown more than once to achieve 
full visual coverage. 
Results 
From June 25-29, 2015 we flew surveys on Mt. Deveber (I), Llama-Turret (H), North Persimmon 
(C), Monoghan (E), Rockslide (F) and South Persimmon (C) for a total a total survey effort of 30.2 
hrs flying time. In total, 277 goats were observed from 59 independent groups. Of the 200 adult 
goats observed, 27 were classified as billies and 49 were classified as nannies.  We observed 27 
yearlings and 47 kids, and only 3 goats that could not be classified by age or sex. These totals are 
broken down by complex in Table 1.
